title: Shoo Fly Don't Bother Me
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a discussion of the 1958 film The Fly and the 1986 Cronenberg remake, then turn to the housefly (Musca domestica). They cover house fly anatomy (compound eyes, ocelli, antennae, proboscis and labellum, halters, wings, tarsi and pulvilli, reproductive organs), the fact that houseflies do not bite, how they eat by vomiting digestive saliva onto food and storing it in the crop, their life cycle from egg to maggot to pupa to adult, diapause, lifespan, the ecological and practical uses of flies, ancient fly-god sacrifices, and ways to control flies. The episode ends with listener mail about a Scooby-Doo college reference and a back-and-forth over Massachusetts colleges, with a mention of Judge John Hodgman.
topics: fly feeding and vomiting digestive juice

segments.title: Opening banter and The Fly films
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about the 1958 film The Fly starring Vincent Price and the Cronenberg remake, then introduce the episode on the housefly and set up the plan to cover fly facts.

segments.title: Housefly anatomy: eyes, ocelli, head
segments.summary: Chuck describes the three body sections and the compound eyes made of thousands of simple eyes, plus the ocelli used as a compass toward sunlight. This is fly fact one, which explains why flies cluster at windows. The head holds antennae, proboscis, labellum and palps.

segments.title: Houseflies do not bite; wings and halters
segments.summary: Fly fact two: houseflies do not bite, and biting flies are horseflies or stable flies. The hosts discuss the two wings and the small halters that help balance and steer, and the wings' flap rate and speed.

segments.title: Legs, tarsi and pulvilli
segments.summary: The thorax holds the wings and legs. Tarsal hairs act like taste buds, and pulvilli are moist suction pads that let flies walk up walls. The abdomen contains reproductive organs that retract when not in use.

segments.title: How flies eat: vomiting digestive juice and the crop
segments.summary: Flies can only take in liquids through the labellum. For solid food they spit digestive saliva onto it, break it down, and store partly digested food in the crop until it is liquid enough. Fly fact three covers the crop. The hosts discuss the disease risk of flies landing on food.

segments.title: Mating, egg laying and the life cycle
segments.summary: Males chase and mate with females quickly, after which they separate and the female lays eggs in a safe place without guarding them. The life cycle runs egg, larva (maggot), pupa, adult, taking about seven to ten days in warm weather. Chuck tells a story of a maggot infestation from a garbage can. Larvae breathe through their rear ends and molt three times. Adults use a temporary swollen bump on the head to crack out of the shell.

segments.title: Diapause and fly lifespan
segments.summary: Fly fact four: diapause is a suspended state in which a fly shuts down life processes when food and predators are scarce, lasting a few months. Average adult lifespan is about twenty-one days, and flies thrive in warm, muggy weather.

segments.title: Ecological value of flies, ancient fly gods, and control
segments.summary: Flies are a protein source for animals, break down material for other organisms, and are used in fish farming through maggots and pupae. Fly fact five says ancient civilizations sacrificed to fly gods. Control methods include keeping a clean house, spiders, parasitic wasps such as the Tara Melody wasp, closed windows, swatters, fly paper, and pesticides, which the hosts do not endorse. Bug zappers are mentioned.

segments.title: Listener mail: Massachusetts colleges and the Hodgman exchange
segments.summary: The hosts read a listener complaint about their statement that the five Scooby-Doo colleges are Boston-area schools. The colleges are Amherst, Mount Holyoke, Smith, and Hampshire, all in the Pioneer Valley of western Massachusetts. Judge John Hodgman exchanges a playful back-and-forth with Chuck, which the hosts read on air.

segments.title: Outro and contact information
segments.summary: The hosts give contact details for Facebook, Twitter, and email, and mention the HowStuffWorks iPhone app and sponsor tagline.
